workflow.critical: Execute through {project-root}/_arcwright/core/tasks/workflow.xml with {installed_path}/workflow.yaml loaded. User and host instructions govern scope, permissions, language, and interaction mode.
Implement the specified story, or the next ready story when requested. A single-story request does not authorize another story, an epic, a retrospective, a push, or a release.
Reuse the shared agent runtime, applicable AGENTS.md, and configuration already in context. Skills provide procedures within those instructions.

step.goal: Resolve the assigned story and context
step.action: Use supplied story_path or story_file. When the user requested the next ready story, select the first ready-for-dev entry in sprint_status order. Ask only if the target remains consequentially ambiguous or unavailable.

Read the selected story once: story_key, epic/story IDs, acceptance criteria, tasks, status, is_ui_story, research_context_file, Dev Notes, and File List. Determine UI scope from requirements, not the presence of UX docs.

Reuse relevant research context with verifiable source paths/content identities. Read original artifacts only for missing, changed, or uncertain facts; cache age alone does not require a reload prompt.

Select relevant skills from catalog metadata or the installed arcwright router. Read selected entrypoints once and only needed references. Do not preload every keyword match. Load test-quality for test authoring/review; load domain/UI guidance only when relevant.
Read {project-root}/_arcwright/awm/resources/review-scope.md for branch/commit/worktree scope. Preserve unrelated workspace edits without stashing or discarding them.
If tasks are already complete, verify current implementation and evidence before selecting remaining work; do not restart completed work.

Set the selected story to in-progress. If sprint_status exists, update only its matching entry, preserving comments, order, and other stories. Do not create sprint tracking merely to run this workflow.

Keep source edits within the assigned story. Maintain story checkboxes, implementation/debug notes, File List, Change Log, Status, and Invoked Skills; do not rewrite agreed requirements without authorization.
Work through incomplete tasks in dependency order. Reuse existing patterns/functionality and make the smallest change that satisfies the acceptance criteria.

Follow test-quality: reuse suitable tests/fixtures, add cases only for plausible defects in changed public behavior, and skip cosmetic/documentation-only tests without a concrete risk. Existing coverage may suffice.
Reproduce regressions before fixing them when feasible. Use red-green-refactor when TDD is requested or selected; do not require a new failing test for every task or subtask.

Run affected tests after relevant changes. Record actual commands, selected cases, results, and source/input identity. Zero selection, skipped/interrupted runs, and stale results are not passing evidence.
For UI/runtime changes, inspect running behavior when practical using host browser/device/evidence tools. Report unavailable checks; mocked tests do not establish runtime proof.
Update actual changed files and concise notes. Mark a task complete only with implementation and appropriate observed verification; it need not own a new test file.
Continue assigned work without milestone confirmation prompts. Ask only for consequential missing requirements, actions outside authorization, or blockers that cannot be resolved independently.

Review the task diff and relevant integration paths against acceptance criteria, correctness, security, failure handling, performance risks, and test quality. Include changed configuration/workflow instructions when they are the product under review.
Report concrete findings with location, evidence, impact, and severity. No minimum finding count applies. A clean review is valid; speculative improvements and style preferences are optional.

check.if: independent review is required by the user, project, or selected workflow
check.action: Use installed subagent-protocol with source identity, relevant skill paths/finder, constraints, and existing evidence. Choose the smallest reviewer set covering distinct material risks; do not dispatch every agent or one per artifact.

If this stage invokes review-loop, follow that skill including its initial model choice. Otherwise honor current model/provider policy. Required independent review that is unavailable or disallowed remains pending; self-review does not replace it.

step.action: Deduplicate actual findings. Keep a compact ledger of fixed, declined-with-reason, disputed, and open items. Save a report only when useful, in the active project's Arcwright output or host evidence storage.

step.goal: Fix confirmed issues and finish required validation
step.action: Fix confirmed in-scope defects in severity order and verify affected behavior. Severity alone does not require approval for an authorized repair. Do not auto-apply unrelated refactors or every optional nit.

Honor the selected review budget; absent another budget, allow up to three review/fix rounds total. Re-review changed code and open findings only; stop when material findings are resolved or only optional nits remain. Budget exhaustion is not approval.

Run affected tests first, then repository-required gates. Reuse checks bound to unchanged source/inputs. Repeat or broaden only for changed code, failures, unresolved risk, or repository requirements. Do not start a QA agent merely to run routine tests.

Separate pre-existing failures from regressions without weakening checks or changing unrelated work. Keep failed/unrun gates and pending required review visible. Apply {installed_path}/checklist.md; no final all-agent review or extra full-suite run is required merely for reaching this step.

step.goal: Report and close the assigned story
step.action: Record actual changes, decisions, verification, useful invoked skills, and unresolved work concisely. Omit model names, attribution labels, coauthor trailers, and generated-by notices; preserve required legal/source credits.

check.if: all acceptance criteria and required implementation, review, and validation gates are satisfied
check.action: Mark verified tasks complete and story Status done. Sync only the matching sprint entry when present.

check.if: a required review, validation gate, or acceptance criterion remains pending or failed
check.action: Keep incomplete tasks unchecked. Use review when implementation is complete but required review is pending, otherwise in-progress. Record the exact blocker and sync the matching sprint entry when present.

step.output: Report story_key, status, changed behavior/files, observed checks, and remaining blockers. State unrun checks accurately.
step.action: Return control after this story. Only an explicitly authorized batch/epic/sprint orchestrator may advance to another story or request a retrospective; return its result and remaining authorized queue without expanding that queue.
